question: What would Trump's last two years look like if Democrats win Congress on 3 November?

lines.text: Democrats need a net gain of just 3 seats to take the House on 3 November, Ballotpedia says.
Nate Silver's model has Democrats ahead by 8.9 points on the generic ballot among likely voters.

scene.label: generic ballot, likely voters
scene.detail: a lead in polls, not a result

lines.text: Win the House, and Democrats take the committees, the gavels and the power to subpoena.
It has happened before. In 2018, Democrats flipped 41 House seats in Trump's first term.

scene.label: House seats flipped, 2018
scene.detail: largest midterm vote margin on record

lines.text: That winter, a fight over border wall money shut the government for 35 days.
In December 2019, the Democratic House impeached him, 230 votes to 197.
But removal needs a two thirds Senate vote. He was acquitted in February 2020.
Divided government can also deal. That same House passed his USMCA trade pact, 385 to 41.
The Senate is harder. Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats, and Democrats need a net gain of 4.
So the next two years could turn on 3 seats, and a veto only two thirds of Congress can override.

sources.title: Democrats won the House with the largest midterms margin of all time
Factbox: The longest US government shutdowns
President Donald Trump impeached for the first time
House passes Trump's USMCA trade agreement

caption: What happens to Trump's last two years if Democrats win Congress in November? A look at the numbers, and at what happened last time. A scenario based on precedent, not a prediction.
